title: Estrategia de pruebas con pytest
review_contracts: PYARCANA — MODO REVISOR ESCÉPTICO Y ANTI-COMPLACENCIA
Solarized Website Content Comprehension Auditor & Rewriter

prior_audit.method: Direct fetch of audit/lessons-only/sections/S27.json returned 404 before creation.

learner_entry_state.critical_dependency_warning: S26 remains REPAIR_REQUIRED and its N2/CF-2 evidence was partly hardcoded. S27 must not treat Level-2 promotion or prior success/approved labels as facts merely because the roadmap names Nivel 2 as prerequisite.
carry_forward_test_targets: final approval must bind exact draft hash and recipient set
idempotency must survive same/different payload and concurrent/restart cases
E2E promotion must be derived from observed manifests rather than hardcoded success

roadmap_expectation.T1: Diseño: riesgos y pirámide; Arrange–Act–Assert y oráculos confiables
roadmap_expectation.T2: Pytest: discovery/assertions y parametrización; fixtures, scopes y aislamiento
roadmap_expectation.T3: Bordes: excepciones, floats, fechas y archivos temporales; casos negativos y mensajes
roadmap_expectation.T4: Cobertura: branch/risk coverage; mutación conceptual, fallas útiles y mantenimiento
roadmap_expectation.gate: convertir supuestos de normalización y matching en contratos ejecutables; cada bug reproducido obtiene test de regresión

live_site.evidence: Public page exposes Section 27 'Pytest y contratos' with the same executable-contract/regression-test tagline. Full hydrated theory is not exposed by the public text surface, so render-only defects were not invented.

checks: A real pytest run based on T2-A returned exit code 0 and '2 passed' while a deliberately wrong plain-loop parameter row produced param_ok=False, proving that the pseudo-parametrized table is not a pytest contract.
parse_score accepts nan, inf, -0.1 and 1.5 instead of rejecting non-finite/out-of-range matching scores.
NamedTemporaryFile(delete=False) remains on disk after the canonical demo unless manually unlinked; the demo does not clean it.
The T4-A manual business-branch counter reports 3/3 both for the canonical >=0.9 threshold and for a behavior-changing mutant >0.9.
classify_pair(float('nan')) silently returns non_match because both comparisons are false.

external_research.finding: Default discovery includes test_*.py/*_test.py, test-prefixed functions, and methods in Test-prefixed classes without __init__; names can be configured.
Fixture scopes are function, class, module, package and session; function is default. Fixtures support teardown and factories.
pytest.raises(match=...) uses re.search; parametrize creates separate invocations/ids; tmp_path is unique per test invocation.
Branch coverage is measured from source-to-destination execution opportunities and enabled with branch measurement; manual output-category counters are not branch coverage.
Mutation testing changes production code and runs the test suite to determine whether tests fail; directly comparing a mutant output to an oracle does not show that the suite killed the mutant.
.test, .example, .invalid and example.com/net/org are special-use; example.pe is not on the registry.

findings.evidence: S27 declares Nivel 2 as prerequisite and opens as if the S26 pipeline and its prior contracts can simply be assumed.
findings.attack: S26 is REPAIR_REQUIRED and its promotion evidence includes hardcoded success/pass values.
findings.defense: A new level needs a narrative bridge from earlier work.
findings.impact: Known false-green states can be treated as trusted test fixtures and laundered into N3.
findings.repair: State that Level-2 artifacts are untrusted until regression manifests pass; make known S26 defects first-class regression targets.

findings.evidence: Opening/callouts/code repeatedly use @example.pe and call those contacts safe synthetic data.
findings.attack: IANA reserves .test/.example/.invalid and example.com/net/org, not example.pe.
findings.defense: The theory examples do not send mail.
findings.impact: Fixtures copied into later integration tests can target a routable namespace while being described as safe synthetic.
findings.repair: Use ana@equipo.test, example.com, or another reserved documentation/test domain consistently.

findings.evidence: Core theory repeatedly substitutes plain Python for pytest: simulated fixture helper, custom assert_raises, manual table loops, manual branch counters; no canonical theory output shows a real pytest collection/failure/pass cycle.
findings.attack: The section is explicitly 'Estrategia de pruebas con pytest' and the roadmap says pytest becomes systematic from S27.
findings.defense: Plain-Python analogies keep browser/runtime examples portable.
findings.impact: Learner can complete theory without learning pytest's actual collection, parametrization, fixtures, failure reporting or lifecycle.
findings.repair: Require pytest in the local venv and execute at least one real test module per T2/T3/T4 contract, keeping simulations only as explanatory precursors.

findings.evidence: Opening says a test that never failed has not proved that it knows how to detect anything.
findings.attack: That is defensible for a regression reproducer but overbroad for newly specified behavior or straightforward invariant tests.
findings.defense: The sentence strongly encourages red-green discipline and mutation sensitivity.
findings.impact: Learner may think every valid new test must historically fail before it has evidentiary value.
findings.repair: Scope the rule to bug regression and explain mutation/fault injection as one way to validate sensitivity for other tests.

findings.evidence: Reference says T4 closes with branch coverage but omits the roadmap's second T4 half: conceptual mutation, useful failures and maintenance.
findings.attack: The reference block is supposed to define section order/scope.
findings.defense: The omitted material appears later in theory.
findings.impact: The learner's advance organizer understates a major closing competence.
findings.repair: Name both branch/risk coverage and mutation/failure/maintenance in the T4 reference sentence.

findings.evidence: Theory says risk changes time allocation 'not the form of the pyramid' and prescribes the pyramid as fixed.
findings.attack: Best-practice material describes the pyramid as a rule of thumb and explicitly notes its simplifications; high-level tests are appropriate when they provide confidence unavailable below.
findings.defense: Many small tests and fewer high-level tests is a useful default heuristic.
findings.impact: A heuristic becomes doctrine and can discourage integration/E2E tests that cover unique failure surfaces.
findings.repair: Present the pyramid as a default cost/confidence heuristic; add tests at the lowest layer that can prove the behavior, moving upward where lower layers cannot.

findings.evidence: Risk score impact×likelihood is mapped to exact quotas: >=15 means >=5 tests; 8–14 means 2–3; <8 means smoke+negative.
findings.attack: No calibration, evidence or project-specific rationale supports those numeric cutoffs or counts.
findings.defense: The paragraph calls the score a practical, non-scientific prioritization device.
findings.impact: Learners may optimize test counts to an invented formula rather than reason about failure modes and confidence.
findings.repair: Keep qualitative risk ranking; derive concrete cases from failure modes/branches and record rationale instead of fixed quotas.

findings.evidence: Theory densely mixes clerical queue, merge, drift, smoke, retro, flake, node id, factory, scope, raw, mock, CI and contract without always introducing Spanish-first meanings.
findings.attack: The reader model is competent but not the author; several terms carry process meaning beyond literal translation.
findings.defense: S27 begins the advanced integration phase and some terms were seen earlier.
findings.impact: Language switching competes with the testing concepts being learned.
findings.repair: Introduce Spanish-first meanings once (cola de revisión manual, prueba mínima/smoke, identificador de caso/node id, etc.) and then retain API literals.

findings.evidence: T1-B offers 'longitud >= 0 tras normalizar' as an invariant oracle.
findings.attack: For any returned string, length>=0 is tautologically true and cannot detect meaningful normalization regressions.
findings.defense: The paragraph also gives useful fixed-value and idempotence oracle examples.
findings.impact: The section teaching reliable oracles includes a property that provides effectively zero fault-detection power.
findings.repair: Replace with nontrivial invariants such as idempotence, no leading/trailing whitespace, single internal whitespace policy, and explicit empty-input behavior.

findings.evidence: T1-B lists 'red o disco no mockeados' as examples of fragile/flaky oracles.
findings.attack: Real filesystem behavior through tmp_path can be deterministic and is often exactly what an integration test should exercise; mocking disk is not intrinsically safer.
findings.defense: Uncontrolled external I/O can make tests environment-dependent.
findings.impact: Learners can over-mock and remove the boundary they intended to test.
findings.repair: Distinguish uncontrolled external dependencies from controlled local temp filesystem/integration boundaries.

findings.evidence: T2-A says pytest discovers Test* classes but omits the no-__init__ condition and configurability of discovery patterns.
findings.attack: Current pytest docs explicitly require Test-prefixed classes without __init__ under default discovery.
findings.defense: The lesson focuses mainly on function tests and default conventions.
findings.impact: Learner can create a Test* class that pytest silently refuses to collect and not understand why.
findings.repair: State the default conditions precisely and note that configuration can change patterns.

findings.evidence: T2-A's table uses all(...) and prints param_ok; rows are called 'conceptual node ids' but are not pytest invocations and no assert consumes param_ok.
findings.attack: An audit run constructed from the same pattern returned pytest exit code 0/'2 passed' while param_ok=False for a deliberately wrong table row.
findings.defense: The comments show a correct @pytest.mark.parametrize form for local use.
findings.impact: The canonical executable can display a failed contract while the test runner stays green.
findings.repair: Execute the real @pytest.mark.parametrize test with ids and remove the print-only pseudo-parametrization.

findings.evidence: Learning outcome promises deterministic tests for normalize_name and exact_match; canonical code defines no exact_match function and only compares two normalize_name calls inline.
findings.attack: Testing an expression is not a regression contract for a public exact_match implementation/API.
findings.defense: The equality expression models the intended exact-match semantics.
findings.impact: The named production behavior can change independently without the advertised test existing.
findings.repair: Define/import exact_match and test its public behavior, including positive, negative, missing and Unicode cases.

findings.evidence: T2-B says fixtures inject dependencies without globals, but executable theory uses a normal fixture_contacts function backed by global _base_contacts; no @pytest.fixture or factory fixture actually runs.
findings.attack: The lesson's fixture-specific lifecycle/isolation behavior is never demonstrated by pytest.
findings.defense: Comments contain a syntactically correct pytest.fixture example and deepcopy illustrates isolation.
findings.impact: Learner may understand copying data but not how fixture request, scope, teardown or factory lifecycle actually works.
findings.repair: Run real function-scope and session/package fixture tests, including a factory and an intentionally contaminated wide-scope negative fixture.

findings.evidence: Theory lists function/class/module/session scopes and says session should only be used for expensive read-only resources.
findings.attack: Current pytest also supports package scope; wider scopes can safely manage mutable resources when lifecycle/reset semantics are explicit.
findings.defense: Read-only is a conservative novice-safe heuristic.
findings.impact: Reference is technically incomplete and turns a safety heuristic into an absolute API rule.
findings.repair: Include package scope and phrase read-only as a default risk-reduction rule rather than a prohibition.

findings.evidence: T2-B says 'si ves un fallo que solo aparece con -x...' and later correctly says -x neither reorders tests nor causes new failures.
findings.attack: The same paragraph presents an impossible diagnostic cue under normal pytest semantics.
findings.defense: It is trying to distinguish first-failure visibility from order randomization.
findings.impact: Learner can blame -x for order coupling it does not create.
findings.repair: Say -x only truncates observation after the first failure; use explicit random-order runs/seeds to diagnose order dependence.

findings.evidence: T3-A explains that NamedTemporaryFile(delete=False) must be cleaned in finally or replaced by tmp_path, but the canonical code never unlinks the created path.
findings.attack: Runtime validation confirmed the file still existed after the demo.
findings.defense: TemporaryDirectory is cleaned correctly in the previous example.
findings.impact: The example violates the resource-lifecycle contract it just taught.
findings.repair: Use tmp_path in real pytest or unlink the named temporary file in finally.

findings.evidence: T3-B says negative cases include score out of range, but parse_score only rejects blank strings and classify_pair accepts arbitrary floats.
findings.attack: Runtime checks show nan, inf, -0.1 and 1.5 are accepted; NaN silently becomes non_match.
findings.defense: parse_score is introduced only to demonstrate exception testing, not as a complete business validator.
findings.impact: The section explicitly names a high-risk negative class without providing the regression contract, and invalid scores can reach threshold logic.
findings.repair: Validate finite score and allowed range before classification; parameterize blank, malformed, NaN, infinity, negative and >1 inputs.

findings.evidence: Theory broadly says matching probabilities should use isclose rather than equality and places this next to threshold decisions.
findings.attack: Approximate equality is appropriate for computed numeric expectations, but threshold branch semantics themselves require exact boundary tests (at, just below, just above).
findings.defense: The code uses explicit tolerances and does not directly apply isclose inside classify_pair.
findings.impact: Learner may blur numerical tolerance with the business definition of a threshold boundary.
findings.repair: Separate value-approximation tests from threshold classification tests and show both patterns.

findings.evidence: T3-B promises None, empty, wrong type, broken encoding and score-out-of-range coverage, but canonical executable tests only four require_email cases.
findings.attack: Several named failure classes have no executable contract in the section where they are introduced.
findings.defense: The paragraph says design a table and examples are illustrative rather than exhaustive.
findings.impact: Learner can believe edge coverage exists because the prose enumerates it even though the suite does not.
findings.repair: Add parameterized negative tables for each public function, especially score finite/range, Unicode/encoding boundary and None/wrong type.

findings.evidence: negative_messages.py accumulates booleans and only prints neg_ok; it never asserts all(results).
findings.attack: A wrong row can produce neg_ok False without failing the process/test runner.
findings.defense: The canonical fixed rows currently evaluate True.
findings.impact: The anti-pattern is identical to the print-only contract the section warns against.
findings.repair: Convert rows to pytest.parametrize and assert the expected exception/value per invocation.

findings.evidence: Theory mandates at least one happy and three negative cases per public function.
findings.attack: The number of meaningful negative cases depends on the contract/failure modes; three can be insufficient or wasteful.
findings.defense: A minimum helps novices remember to test failures.
findings.impact: Learners may count cases rather than enumerate contract partitions and risks.
findings.repair: Require coverage of identified input partitions/failure modes, with a small minimum only as a scaffold if explicitly labeled heuristic.

findings.evidence: T4-A calls the topic branch coverage but executable code manually increments auto/review/non counters; it never enables Coverage.py branch measurement or consumes a report.
findings.attack: Coverage.py defines branch coverage as observed source-to-destination execution opportunities; output categories are not equivalent.
findings.defense: The manual counters visualize business branch coverage without adding a dependency.
findings.impact: Learner can report 'branch coverage' without measuring code branches at all.
findings.repair: Use coverage.py/pytest-cov with branch measurement, then separately track business-risk scenario coverage.

findings.evidence: T4-A uses [0.95,0.7,0.2,0.9] and reports 3/3 outcomes; it omits the 0.6 boundary, just-below/above boundaries and invalid/nonfinite scores.
findings.attack: A mutation from score>=0.9 to score>0.9 changed the 0.9 result but the manual counter still reported 3/3.
findings.defense: 0.9 at least includes one exact boundary case.
findings.impact: The metric stays green while a high-risk threshold contract changes.
findings.repair: Parameterize each boundary at/just below/just above and invalid values; assert exact labels independently of branch-count metrics.

findings.evidence: Coverage callout says if review branch is never tested, the review queue 'se romperá en producción'.
findings.attack: Untested code is higher risk but failure is not logically guaranteed.
findings.defense: The warning is intended to motivate risk-based testing.
findings.impact: Overclaim weakens epistemic discipline in a section about evidence.
findings.repair: Use 'puede romperse sin que CI lo detecte' and keep the causal claim bounded.

findings.evidence: mutation_useful.py sets mutation_killed = normalize_name_mutated(raw) != oracle; it never runs the test suite against the mutant.
findings.attack: Mutation testing defines a killed mutant by a test failing when mutated production code runs.
findings.defense: The section explicitly says conceptual/manual mutation is acceptable initially.
findings.impact: A direct output comparison is labeled as evidence that the suite protects the contract, which it does not demonstrate.
findings.repair: Inject/swap the implementation under test and show an actual pytest failure; optionally use mutmut later.

findings.evidence: Opening/gate repeatedly require bug_repro -> failing regression -> fix -> passing regression, but no canonical theory example shows a known bug failing before the repair and passing afterward.
findings.attack: The defining section behavior is asserted, not demonstrated.
findings.defense: Mutation example is intended to show a failure-sensitive contract conceptually.
findings.impact: Learner never sees the evidence sequence that distinguishes a regression test from a post-hoc green test.
findings.repair: Include one real red-green bug reproduction with captured pytest failure output, repair, rerun and permanent regression test.

findings.evidence: S27 teaches risk-first testing but ignores the known high-severity S26 failures carried into the continuation ledger and spends theory on toy normalize/email examples instead.
findings.attack: The campaign already knows concrete partial-cycle, HITL-gate, idempotency, persistence and hardcoded-E2E defects—exactly the highest-value regression targets.
findings.defense: Roadmap defines S27 as start CP-N3-A focused on normalización/matching rather than retrofitting S26.
findings.impact: The course's own risk-first rule is not applied at the level transition, and N2 defects can remain green while N3 starts.
findings.repair: Add a small inherited-regression pack for Level-2 gates before CP-N3-A tests; then proceed to normalize/matching.

findings.evidence: Job relevance lists unit/contract/integration as layers while the section uses 'contrato' mainly to mean behavioral promise and the roadmap pyramid is unit/integration/E2E.
findings.attack: 'Contract test' is also a distinct testing category in common practice, so the term changes meaning without clarification.
findings.defense: In Spanish prose 'contrato ejecutable' is a useful metaphor for assertions.
findings.impact: Learner may confuse behavioral contract tests with consumer/provider interface contract testing.
findings.repair: Define 'contrato de comportamiento' for this section and reserve 'contract test' for interface/provider-consumer testing when introduced.

findings.evidence: S27-aaa-oracle alt says the oracle 'enters' after Act and also omits accents in 'despues/oraculo'.
findings.attack: Expected behavior should be chosen independently before observing the Act result; placing the oracle after Act risks encouraging derivation from current output, the exact anti-pattern the section warns against.
findings.defense: Visually, Assert occurs after Act and consumes the oracle there.
findings.impact: The only AAA diagram can encode the wrong temporal model of when expected truth is established.
findings.repair: Show expected/oracle defined in Arrange, Act producing actual, and Assert comparing actual to expected; fix Spanish accents in alt text.

rejected_findings: pytest.raises(match=...) using regex was not a defect; current pytest documentation confirms re.search semantics and re.escape for literal metacharacters.
math.isclose was not rejected as a float-testing tool; the defect is failing to distinguish approximate numeric equality from exact business threshold boundaries.
Manual mutation itself was not rejected; the defect is calling a direct mutant-output comparison evidence that the test suite killed the mutant.
Using tmp_path/tempfile was not rejected; the defect is the delete=False example violating its own cleanup rule.

usable: fixed independent oracles instead of copying current output
function-scope isolation as a safe default
clock injection for deterministic date logic
approximate comparison for computed floating values with explicit tolerances
branch coverage is not the same as line coverage
mutation testing asks whether tests detect behavior-changing mutations
bug reproduction should become a permanent regression contract
misconception_risk: @example.pe is a safely reserved synthetic email domain
a plain loop row is a pytest node id
printing param_ok/neg_ok is an executable test contract
length>=0 is a useful normalization invariant
branch outcome counters equal Coverage.py branch coverage
3/3 business outcomes proves threshold boundaries are protected
mutant_output != oracle means the test suite killed the mutant
session fixtures are an API-level read-only-only feature
any matching float comparison should use tolerance, including business threshold semantics
